$comment: The benchmark fixture: 9 positions, 3 per phase, committed so the x86/ARM comparison
is reproducible rather than another ad hoc run (docs/beta-readiness.md §6).
Depth reached at a fixed budget varies enormously by phase — depth 26 in a middlegame
against 55 in an endgame at the same 5s budget (.claude/rules/engine-contract.md) — so
results are reported per phase and never pooled. That is also why the phase label is
part of the committed data and not inferred at run time from piece count: a position's
phase is a claim this fixture makes, and it should be reviewable in the diff.
Positions are chosen to be quiet and non-terminal. A position with a forced mate in
view resolves early and stops iterating, which measures the mate distance rather than
